summary: Executed the selected reproduction step in a disposable copy with a median-of-three timing matrix. Recipe: build input = 'a'.repeat(n) + ' '.repeat(n) + '!', parse it in strict and permissive modes for n from 2000 to 64000, and compare with 'a'.repeat(n) + '!' and 'name=' + 'a'.repeat(n) + ' '.repeat(n). Strict time rose from about 2.4 ms at n=2000 to about 2.3 s at n=64000, roughly fourfold per doubling; permissive mode behaved the same. A 250000-character fixture under a five-second external timeout was terminated. The no-whitespace name and the early-equals value tail stayed near 0.1 ms at n=64000. Adding '; Path=/' after the pathological prefix left timing unchanged, so semicolon stripping and attribute parsing were not the sink. Strict mode returned no cookie for the no-equals fixture; permissive mode returned an empty key and the full value, matching the overlapping optional-group semantics. This supports the quadratic pair-split hypothesis and contradicts the strict-only framing. Evidence is a local causal result, not an official harness result. Limits: one process and one machine, one input family, and no patched comparison yet.
next_hint: Both strict and permissive pair paths are quadratic, and the sink is before attribute parsing. Determine the exact deterministic split semantics for empty names, leading and multiple equals signs, whitespace after the separator, and newline/carriage-return/null value termination, then build a baseline-versus-patch differential before trusting a repair.
